whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text: This series partially arose from my work as a critical care nurse. Working nights in the neurosurgical ICU, one becomes very aware of the sounds in the room. The constant noise of the machines, the ventilators breathing for the patients and keeping them alive. And I had the idea for little scared holographic ghosts rising up from the patients and the machines into the darkened room. I stress the quality of the holographic image in my work and how that interacts with other materials. In these pieces, the transparency and fragility of the image works to express a reality in our own lives. That we all live in a very transparent world. In a transitional state. The medium is appropriate. The holographic images, fragile and fleeting, mirror the transitory and elusive nature of our own threatened lives. That has been a thing for me. This idea of fragility. And I think that's why I like using the hologram with the figures. You know, you're making that little fragile figure even more fragile by using the hologram. GIVING GIVING
